answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether buying ivory paint, sourcing lantern oil, or scheduling deliveries at dawn. Each bonded identity gets the same bidding quota, so spawning accounts cannot create free capacity: an attacker seeking 1,000 quotas must immobilize $100,000 for a month, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital throughout the lock.
